title: Revert "[kernel] add fused silu mul quant fp8" (#38381)
body:
Reverts sgl-project/sglang#37376

## Why

#37376 enables a fused silu+mul+FP8-quant kernel on the block-wise FP8 MoE path. It is not numerically equivalent to the two-kernel path it replaces, and the difference is large enough to cost speculative-decoding acceptance on GLM-5.2-FP8 EAGLE MTP.

`test/registered/e2e/models/test_dsa_glm52_tp_mtp.py::test_bs_1_speed` asserts `accept_length > 4.0` and is currently failing on main.

## Bisect

Two `Rerun Test` dispatches of that test on the `8-gpu-h200` pool, at #37376 and its direct parent:

| commit | Acc Length | Tokens | Speed (token/s) | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `503511c963` (parent) | **4.727** | 1092 | 323.28 | pass |
| `a8b2f36dee` (#37376) | **3.949** | 778 | 265.40 | fail |

- [run at parent](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34173127970) / [run at #37376](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34173132321)
- 4.727 is the value every scheduled main run produced before #37376 landed; 3.949 reproduces identically across all three attempts in the run.
- Net effect on this recipe: **-16.5% accept length, -18% bs=1 decode speed**.

## Mechanism

- `_can_use_fused_silu_mul_quant_fp8` turns the kernel on from shape/dtype alone. There is no flag or env var to disable it, so an affected model cannot opt out.
- The fused kernel emits the FP8 down-GEMM input directly, skipping the bf16 `intermediate_cache2` round-trip, so its output differs from the two-kernel path.
- The unit test added in #37376 states the tolerance explicitly: `fp8_match > 0.95` (up to 5% of FP8 bytes may differ) and `assert_close(fused_output, fallback_output, rtol=0.02, atol=0.02)`.
- Accuracy-style evals absorb that (`cosine_sim > 0.9999`), but acceptance length is a discrete draft/target token-agreement rate compounded over 5 draft steps, and target and draft share the same MoE, so the perturbation accumulates instead of averaging out.

## Note

Reverting rather than gating because no switch exists today. A reland could keep the kernel behind an opt-in flag, or disable it when speculative decoding is enabled.

title: [AMD][GLM-5.2] Keep GlmMoeDsa MoE e_score_correction_bias in fp32 (#37133)
body:
## Problem

GLM-5.2's MoE scores experts with `sigmoid(logits) + e_score_correction_bias` and takes the top 8.

That bias is fp32 in the checkpoint, with values in [6.817, 7.063] — a spread of 0.246 sitting up at 7. Near 7, bf16's smallest step is 0.03125, so it can only represent about 8 distinct values there. `MoEGate.__init__` casts the parameter to bf16 whenever a quant_config is present, so 238 distinct biases collapse into 8.

The result is that the wrong experts get picked. Routing the same real gating output both ways, 98.5% of tokens select a different top-8 set. HF keeps this tensor in fp32.

## Change

Two places have to change together:

1. `MoEGate.__init__`: skip the bf16 cast for GLM-5.2.
2. `biased_grouped_topk_gpu`, aiter path: it cast the bias back down before the kernel call. Keep an fp32 bias in fp32 and upcast the gating logits instead. This is gated on the bias dtype, not the architecture, so a model whose bias is already bf16 is unchanged.

## Cost

8k in / 1k out, MI355X, TP8, concurrency 32, two reps per arm:

| output tok/s | this PR | parent | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| MTP off | 947.6 | 977.5 | -3.06% |
| MTP on | 1338.4 | 1323.7 | within noise |

3% slower without MTP. With MTP there is no measurable difference — the parent arm's own two reps differ by 18.1, more than the 14.7 between arms.

The overhead is per gating call, independent of how many tokens that forward produces. Without MTP one token carries all of it; with MTP the accept length is 5.13, so the same call is spread over ~5 tokens.

## Accuracy

Standard benchmarks cannot see this (GSM8K 0.941 → 0.947, GPQA-Diamond 0.8333 → 0.8182, both within error bars) — MoE experts are redundant, so the wrong expert often still gives the right answer. This is a routing-correctness fix, not a benchmark win.

title: Keep fp32 routing weights in the fp8 block-scale and bf16 trtllm MoE (#33631)
body:
The packed `topk_ids` format is `(expert_id << 16) | bf16(weight)`, so the routed fp8 block-scale and bf16 paths truncate the fp32 routing weights the router produced. Pass the ids and weights unpacked instead, as the mxfp4 path does in #33608.

The fused gate emits packed ids directly, and those already carry bf16 weights, so that case keeps the packed form.

The nvfp4 `fused_experts_none_to_flashinfer_trtllm_fp4` call site was the last one still packing, so it is converted too; `_get_packed_topk_ids_for_flashinfer_routed` then has no callers and goes away. That drops the prepacked fast path it took via `getattr(topk_output, "packed_topk_ids")` — `StandardTopKOutputPacked` reports the standard format, so the fused topk+pack carrier now feeds the kernel its fp32 `topk_weights` instead of the bf16-truncated packed ids.

Needs flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4352, which shipped in flashinfer 0.6.18 — already pinned on main since #36954.

title: MiniMax-M3: Triton split-K router GEMV with in-kernel fixup (#36557)
body:
# MiniMax-M3: Triton split-K router GEMV with in-kernel split-K fixup

The MiniMax-M3 MoE router gate is a skinny GEMV — `[M, K]` bf16 x `[N, K]` bf16 -> `[M, N]` fp32, with `N ~ 128` experts and `M <= 64` at decode — and the vendor BLAS solutions picked for that shape run far off the memory roofline on gfx950 (~0.1 TB/s for a ~1.6MB weight read at `M<=8`, `N=128`). This PR adds `python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/router_gemv.py`, a Triton split-K kernel that reads the gate weight once at near-bandwidth, and routes `MiniMaxM3MoE._compute_router_logits` through it when `router_gemv_supported()` says the shape qualifies. Configs are per-M-bucket (`BLOCK_K` 512 throughout, `BLOCK_N` and `SPLIT_K` chosen by batch size, with a dedicated `BLOCK_M == 1` GEMV path that uses `tl.sum` instead of `tl.dot`) covering `M <= 8 / 16 / 32 / 64`. The split-K reduction is done inside the same kernel: the last CTA to finish a `(n-block, row-tile)` pair reduces all `SPLIT_K` partials and resets its counter slot to zero on the way out, so the scratch buffer stays reusable across launches without either a zero-init launch or a separate reduce launch — each extra launch costs ~2us on gfx950, which is a meaningful fraction of the kernel itself at these sizes. Anything the kernel does not cover — wrong dtype, non-contiguous last dim, `N` not divisible by `BLOCK_N`, `K` not divisible by `BLOCK_K`, or `M > 64` — falls through `router_gemv_supported()` to the existing `torch.mm` path unchanged.

## Performance

title: [Kimi-K3] Accept fp32 routing weights in the fused MoE finalize (#38612)
body:
## Summary

The trtllm-gen deferred finalize returns its routing weights at the dtype the caller passed in, so K3's unpacked `(topk_ids, topk_weights)` routing yields fp32 weights where the packed form yielded bf16. The fused finalize kernel matched bf16 only and a 72-token decode batch killed the server during CUDA-graph capture. #38588 stopped that by casting to bf16 at the call site. This PR makes the kernel take either dtype instead, and reverts the cast.

`finalize_vec` is templated on the routing-weight dtype, the kernel's `kFinalize` bool becomes `typename FinWeight = void`, and the host dispatches on `expert_weights.dtype()` at the `TensorMatcher` that already validates the tensor.

| | #38588 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Weight precision | bf16, rounded before the kernel | fp32 as the router emits it |
| Per call | +2.3 to +11 us | no measurable change |
| Added work per MoE layer | cast launch + alloc before the collective | none |

Per call on 8x B300, best of 3 interleaved repeats of 200 iterations:

| bs | This PR | #38588 | Delta | Spread |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 9.35 us | 18.29 us | -8.94 us | 2.6 / 3.0 |
| 8 | 10.13 us | 19.60 us | -9.48 us | 3.4 / 1.7 |
| 32 | 11.41 us | 22.57 us | -11.15 us | 2.8 / 1.0 |
| 72 | 16.31 us | 18.88 us | -2.57 us | 1.6 / 2.0 |
| 128 | 21.95 us | 24.20 us | -2.25 us | 1.7 / 1.7 |

The routing row is 64 B/token at fp32 against ~114 KB/token of gemm2 gathers, so the wider load is free. The cast's cost is the launch and allocation ahead of the collective, which also skews rank arrival at the push barrier.

Both dtypes are live in production: the packed path caps at 64 tokens (`moe_route_quant_fused.covered`) while the push finalize fits 73, so batches of 65 to 73 defer with fp32 weights.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `test_ar_fusion.py` (8x B300) | 63 passed, `finalize_push_norm` parametrized over both dtypes |
| Same test on the old kernel | 5 fp32 cases fail with the reported dtype error |
| Kimi-K3 B300 Balanced e2e | bs=72 capture clean, GSM8K 0.98 against a 0.95 gate |

title: Fix DeepSeek-V4 routing: sqrtsoftplus underflow and unfloored renorm (#34459)
body:
## Motivation

Similar bug to https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/30989

DeepSeek-V4's `sqrtsoftplus` gate has four routing implementations, and each was missing a different piece of the numerics its reference gate provides (`inference/model.py` `Gate.forward`, `F.softplus`). Same class as flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3803.

1. **Triton router** (default, layers 3-42) computed `log(1.0 + exp(x))`, which in fp32 rounds to `log(1.0) == 0` for `x <= -16.64`. If every top-K expert falls below that, the row renormalizes to all-zero weights and the token loses its entire routed-expert contribution.
2. **`hash_topk`** (layers 0-2) divided by `routed_sum` with no floor, in both the CUDA kernel (default) and its torch fallback. Hash routing ignores scores, so an all-underflowed row gives `0/0` = NaN. Every sibling already floors this.
3. **CUDA `moe_fused_gate`** (test-only) used `log1pf(expf(x))`, which overflows above `88.7`.

On B300: worst relative error vs `F.softplus` over `[-104, 200]` goes `1.0` -> `3.5e-07`; `hash_topk` at `-200` goes `nan` -> `0.0`; `test_moe_fused_gate.py` 39 passed.

title: [JIT] Port the expert-pack MXFP4 kernels to load_jit and fix their launch limits (#38830)
body:
## Summary

`expert_pack_mxfp4` was built with `torch.utils.cpp_extension.load`, whose `FileBaton` waits on a lock **file** and only releases it in a `finally`. A build killed mid-flight leaves the file behind, and every later run against that cache spins on it forever with no output — a 7s test can burn a full CI timeout, and the cache outlives the job. Ported to `load_jit`, which uses `fcntl.flock` (released by the kernel when the holder dies), then fixed three latent bugs the rewritten validation now owns.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Build lock | stale lock file wedges every later run, silently | `flock`, freed on process death |
| `records` → `grid.y` (cap 65535) | 16384 tokens × top-k 4 = 65536, the first failing value → launch aborts at stock settings | `grid.x` (cap 2³¹-1); both dims checked |
| `hidden_size % 64` | partial Marlin tile reads a neighbouring slot *inside* the tensor; memcheck clean, no diagnostic | rejected |
| `role_bytes` in repack | unchecked; inconsistent value silently produced wrong output | asserted, as matvec already did |
| `#pragma once` | absent | added (insurance, not a fix) |

Device kernels unchanged apart from the matvec block-index swap. Public Python API and all callers unchanged.

**Verified on a 5090:** 4 + 11 tests pass; cold JIT rebuild; matvec re-derived against the CPU reference across 1–9 row tiles, both dtypes, the dual path, and up to 200k records; stream binding confirmed by CUDA-graph capture; `pre-commit` clean. `mxfp4_marlin_repack` is test-only, so the two stricter repack checks carry no production risk — all of it sits on the grid fix.

title: [MoE][ROCm] Admit the unified Triton router on ROCm, including single-group routing (#38328)
body:
The opt-in unified Triton router (`SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_KERNEL_GROUPED_TOPK`, off
by default) was gated on CUDA and on more than one expert group. Nothing in the
kernel is CUDA-specific, so admit ROCm and single-group routing. CUDA's condition
is unchanged, and with the flag off every path is byte-identical to before.

Three things follow:

- **Width.** The kernel wants the total top-k, shared slots included, but
  `select_experts` passes `num_routed_topk if _use_aiter else top_k`. Only the
  aiter caller adds the shared slots back.
- **Shared expert once.** `_post_process_topk_ids` appends shared slots for an
  aiter runner; this router emits them itself. Appending again writes the id
  twice and evicts a real routed expert. Now it appends only when the row comes
  back short.
- **Scaling.** An aiter runner skips the post-MoE multiply, so the routed weights
  must carry `routed_scaling_factor` and the shared slot must be 1.0.

`gating_output` loses its torch-side fp32 cast; the kernel widens on load.

## Tests

`test/registered/kernel/moe/test_jit_grouped_topk.py`, 10 cases, registered on
CUDA (`base-b-kernel-unit`) and AMD (`jit-kernel-unit-test-amd`).

Compared against `biased_grouped_topk_impl`, not `select_experts` with the flag
off — on ROCm that is the aiter path, which casts the correction bias down to the
gating dtype, and GLM-5.2 keeps that bias where bf16 cannot separate neighbours.
Measured on MI355X: 8 rows in 256 differ, all by less than one bf16 ULP at that
offset. It reorders routing on its own.

Width is pinned separately for both `_use_aiter` values, since whichever GPU runs
the suite fixes that flag and can only exercise one half.

MI355X / ROCm 7.2: 10 passed. `ruff`, `ruff-format`, `isort`, `codespell` clean.

title: Fix MegaMoE buffer allocation and caching for effective SM budgets (#39223)
body:
## Why is this change needed?

DeepGEMM derives MegaMoE buffer size and layout from the runtime SM count ([buffer sizing](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/blob/66081d4c9c7d7c44f13fea402e5b622aa0f409c2/csrc/apis/mega_moe.hpp#L44)). SGLang applies an SM budget to kernel execution, but previously allocated outside that context and cached without the effective SM count.

For the CPU test's 132-SM ambient count and 130-SM cap:

```diff
- Allocate at 132 SMs; execute at 130.
+ Allocate and execute at 130 SMs.
- Reuse that buffer when an outer context limits execution to 96 SMs.
+ Allocate a separate buffer for the 96-SM budget.
```

The shared helper now allocates under the existing SM context and includes `deep_gemm.get_num_sms()` in the cache key. Equal effective budgets still reuse their buffer. Kernel code, dependencies, and caller APIs are unchanged; distinct budgets can retain additional buffers.

title: [Feature] Support BF16 and batch-invariant inference with DeepEP v2 (#38160)
body:
## Summary

Enable BF16 checkpoints and batch-invariant inference with `--moe-a2a-backend deepep_v2`, and fix a missing-argument error in the existing FP8 prefill path.

The wire dtype follows the expert weights: BF16 experts receive BF16 activations; supported blockwise FP8 experts receive FP8 activations and scales. With `--enable-deterministic-inference`, tokens retain identical results when changes in batch size move them between TP ranks. Decode CUDA graphs remain enabled.

## Changes

### Fix contiguous scatter

#35758 added `expert_start` and `num_experts` to `_fwd_kernel_ep_scatter_2` without updating the DeepEP v2 `ep_scatter_from_psum` caller introduced in #35634. Prefill raises:

```text
TypeError: dynamic_func() missing 2 required positional arguments:
'expert_start' and 'num_experts'
```

Pass `expert_start=0` and the local expert count because DeepEP v2 already rebases received expert IDs. Add CUDA tests for BF16 and FP8 inputs; both fail on the PR base and pass with the fix.

### Support BF16 communication

- Resolve the dispatch dtype from the expert quantization method and reject a conflicting `--deepep-dispatcher-output-dtype`. Require the quantization method when creating the dispatcher so an omitted argument cannot silently select FP8.
- Pass `use_fp8_dispatch` to `ElasticBuffer`, skipping activation quantization for BF16 experts in both prefill and decode.
- Accept scale-free BF16 dispatch output in the DeepGEMM adapter and avoid allocating activation scales for it.
- Admit unquantized BF16 experts while preserving the existing blockwise FP8 contract and DeepGEMM runner requirement.

### Enable batch-invariant inference

The remaining batch dependence was in TP reduce-scatter **before the MoE**. Its floating-point summation order depends on the receiving rank. As a serving batch grows, a token can move to another rank and enter the first MoE layer with different bits.

Under deterministic inference, `GroupCoordinator.reduce_scatter_tensor` now uses the existing deterministic all-reduce path followed by a local slice. It clones the input to preserve the input contract, including callers whose output aliases an input slice. Other modes retain native reduce-scatter.

Remove the DeepEP v2 deterministic-inference rejection. Leave ElasticBuffer receive sorting disabled: expert computation is row-independent and combine follows the handle's slot pointers; the sort's dynamic indexing is also incompatible with decode CUDA graph capture.

title: [misc] Fix tool-call index, graph padded-row count, and prefill-graph input_embeds refresh (#39574)
body:
## Summary

Five independent fixes in the OpenAI chat server, the CUDA graph runners, and the MoE runners. Each is one or two commits and stands on its own.

## Changes

**1. Non-streaming `tool_calls[i].index` is the call ordinal.**
`_process_tool_calls` numbered calls by the detector's `tool_index`, which for most detectors is the tool's position in the request. Two calls to the same tool therefore both got `index=0`, while the streaming deltas number them 0 and 1. The non-streaming path now enumerates the parsed calls. Regression test added in `test_serving_chat.py`.

**2. `num_token_non_padded` is only handed out when it is maintained.**
The decode graph runner allocated the `num_token_non_padded` slot unconditionally, wrote it at capture, and refreshed it at replay only under expert parallelism. Without EP the static ForwardBatch carried a stale capture-time count, while eager batches carry `None` (`ForwardBatch.init_new` only fills it under EP). `DecodeInputBuffers.create` and the dummy-run buffers now allocate the slot only when `enable_num_token_non_padded()`; the capture-time writes are guarded. Graph and eager batches now follow the same rule: no count unless it is live.

**3. The standard MoE path masks padded rows like the a2a path.**
`DeepseekV2MoE.forward_normal` and `forward_normal_dual_stream` pass `forward_batch.num_token_non_padded` into top-k, as `forward_deepep` already does. With EP and the standard dispatcher, padded rows of a CUDA graph batch are now routed to expert id -1 instead of real experts, which also keeps them out of the expert-distribution statistics. Without EP the count is `None` and routing is unchanged. The dual-stream variant is additionally skipped inside a breakable CUDA graph capture, matching the guard the hc path already has.

**4. Prefill CUDA graph replay refreshes the `input_embeds` slot from `input_ids`.**
When the outer forward calls the captured stack without `input_embeds`, the replay closure previously left the slot untouched and the graph read the previous batch's embeddings. It now computes them from `input_ids` via `get_input_embeddings()`.

**5. Deferred finalize accepts fp32 expert weights.**
FlashInfer >= 0.6.18 types the `do_finalize=False` weight buffer by content: bf16 for packed routing, the caller's dtype for unpacked routing. The fp32 -> bf16 bit reinterpretation in `_make_deferred_finalize_output` was only correct for older versions and would corrupt genuine fp32 weights; `moe_finalize_fuse_shared` already accepts both dtypes.

title: [AMD] GLM-5.2 NextN: cast draft fused MoE to per-channel FP8 (#39155)
body:
Re-submission of #38476 on behalf of @fanxingran. The four original commits retain their original author attribution; the original discussion and comments remain on #38476.

## Motivation

Layer 78 of GLM-5.2 is the MTP draft layer. The MXFP4 checkpoint ships its routed
and shared experts in bf16 — 71.7 MB per expert against 19.0 MB for an MXFP4
decoder layer — and MTP reads that layer once per draft step. In bandwidth-bound
decode it therefore costs more than its share of the parameter count suggests.

While wiring the quantized path up it turned out `QuarkW8A8FP8MoE` could never
reach its AITER runner, so every quark per-channel FP8 MoE on ROCm was silently
running Triton.

## Modifications

- **Cast the GLM NextN fused-expert weights to per-channel FP8 at load time**
  (`deepseek_weight_loader.py`), and point quark's per-module scheme selection at
  the matching `QuarkW8A8FP8MoE` scheme (`glm4_moe.py`). Off by default behind
  `SGLANG_GLM_NEXTN_MOE_PTPC`. The loader additionally requires a GLM
  `model_type`: the mixin is shared with DeepSeek, where no matching scheme
  exists and the cast weights would have nowhere to load.

- **Fix the AITER runner selection in `QuarkW8A8FP8MoE`.** The AITER branch was
  gated on `moe_runner_config.apply_router_weight_on_input`, which no model that
  resolves to a quark scheme sets, so the branch was unreachable. Select the
  runner from what the kernel actually requires — per-channel weight scales,
  AITER built in, and an a2a backend that supports it — and route `apply_weights`
  through `AiterMoeQuantInfo`. Preshuffling now keys off the selected runner
  rather than the same dead flag, so the canonical layout is preserved when
  Triton runs.

- **Copy the `QuarkConfig` before the NextN remap** in
  `_resolve_nextn_quant_config`. The caller keeps that object for the target model
  and for `lm_head`, so the draft-only rewrite was mutating shared state. A no-op
  for GLM-5.2-MXFP4, whose `layer_quant_config` is empty, but wrong for any
  checkpoint that sets one.

### On the runner default

`auto` now resolves to AITER for this scheme, matching what its siblings in the
same directory already do — `quark_w4a4_mxfp4_moe.py` and
`quark_w4a8_mxfp4_moe.py` both promote `auto` to AITER when the a2a backend
supports it. `QuarkW8A8FP8MoE` was the one left on Triton, and only because of
the dead flag, so this restores consistency rather than introducing a new default.

title: [Intel XPU] Enable fused_moe_triton tuning on XPU and add tuned DeepSeek-OCR-2 configs (#28723)
body:
## Motivation

Enable `fused_moe_triton` tuning on Intel XPU and ship tuned DeepSeek-OCR-2 MoE
configs for Arc Pro B60.

The `_sep` tuner is CUDA-only: graph capture, events, seeding, and timing go
through `torch.cuda.*` directly, and its ray worker pins every actor to device 0.
This makes it device-agnostic, fixes tuner issues that a full sweep exposes, and
adds the resulting `E=64,N=896` configs under `configs/triton_3_8_0/`.

## Modifications

- Route synchronize / events / seeding / graph capture through `get_device_module`,
  and apply the device id ray assigns each worker. Both follow `tuning_fused_moe_triton.py`.
- Clear the B `TensorDescriptor` cache per config: the tuner allocates fresh weights
  each time, so stale entries pin dead ones and starve graph capture. Inert for
  serving, where weights live for the process lifetime.
- Resolve the `topk_ids` layer layout from the model config instead of DeepSeek-V3's
  hardcoded 61/3, and register `DeepseekOCRForCausalLM` in `common_utils.py`.
- Declare the `ray` extra in `pyproject_xpu.toml`, with `dpctl` that ray's Intel GPU
  detection is gated on; opt-in, not in `all`, so serving installs are unaffected.
- Add tuned `E=64,N=896` configs (full sweep, 18 batch sizes, both projections),
  keyed on shape so they also serve DeepSeek-OCR v1. CUDA serving paths untouched.

## Upstream Triton issues

Both raised from this work against `intel/intel-xpu-backend-for-triton`, both
resolved:

- [#7306](https://github.com/intel/intel-xpu-backend-for-triton/issues/7306) —
  Host-side tensor descriptors drop the 2D-block-I/O fast path on XPU (BMG/CRI).
- [#7691](https://github.com/intel/intel-xpu-backend-for-triton/issues/7691) —
  `TensorDescriptor` shape specialization causes one JIT compile per batch size.

## Kernel results

Time per MoE layer (up + down projection) in microseconds, lower is better.
`E=64, N=896, K=1280, topk=6`, bf16, single Arc Pro B60. Measured with the
tuner's own `--configs` mode, so routing and the serving stack are outside the
timed region.

title: MiniMax-M3: allow shared-experts fusion on ROCm gfx942 and newer (#36576)
body:
# MiniMax-M3: allow shared-experts fusion on ROCm gfx942 and newer

`shared_experts_fusion_disable_reason` currently refuses on any non-CUDA device, so ROCm never gets shared-experts fusion even where the hardware supports it. This lifts that guard and gates it at gfx942 instead.

`minimax_m3_vl.py` carries the identical gate. `MiniMaxM3SparseForCausalLM` and `MiniMaxM3SparseForConditionalGeneration` are separate `EntryClass`es with separate `shared_experts_fusion_disable_reason` classmethods, and the served MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 checkpoint is the **VL** variant (`model_type: minimax_m3_vl`, per `configs/minimax_vl.py`) — so patching only one file would be a silent no-op on the model people actually run.

## Measurement status — stated plainly

**This PR has no benchmark or accuracy numbers of its own, and I am not claiming any.**

The earlier combined change (this gate + the alternate-stream overlap + a `prefill_attention_backend=aiter` serving default) measured +46.6%..+55.4% output throughput on 8x MI350X. That number belongs to the bundle, not to this PR, and decomposing it showed the input-throughput share came **entirely** from the serving default, not from either code change.

More importantly: in every run measured, the server reported `shared_experts_fusion=False` on both sides — the fusion this PR enables **never actually engaged**, because it also requires the model config and serving flags to request it. So the throughput effect of *this* gate specifically is unmeasured.

What this PR is, therefore, is an enablement gate: it removes a platform restriction that has no reason to exist on gfx942+. It should be reviewed on that basis, and someone with a configuration that genuinely turns fusion on should measure it before it is treated as a performance change.

The serving-defaults and cookbook half is a separate change and is not part of this PR.

title: [Moe] Fix flashinfer_trtllm silently dropping swiglu_limit clamped SwiGLU activation (#39920)
linked_issues: #39797 [Question] GLM-5.3-Flash on 4x GB200: `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm` scores ~1.3 gsm8k points below `deep_gemm` in repeated runs (6 vs 3 runs); one `triton` run agrees with deep_gemm
body:
## Motivation

Models with a clamped SwiGLU activation (e.g. GLM-5.3-Flash / GLM-5-Next, Qwen3-Next style) plumb the clamp limit through `FusedMoE(swiglu_limit=...)` -> `MoeRunnerConfig.swiglu_limit`. All MoE runner backends are supposed to honor it: `triton` passes it into the fused kernel, `deep_gemm` applies it via `silu_and_mul_clamp` / `_apply_swiglu_limit`, but `flashinfer_trtllm` **silently ignores it**.

The flashinfer_trtllm FP8 path only materializes `gemm1_clamp_limit` (the TRT-LLM kernel parameter), which stays `None` for models that use the `swiglu_limit` field. With no error and no warning, the expert activation degrades from the trained `silu(clamp(gate, max=L)) * clamp(up, -L, L)` (with L = 10.0) to a plain `silu(gate) * up`, which measurably hurts accuracy.

On GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 (blockwise 128x128 FP8, 288 routed experts, top-8, 1 shared expert, `swiglu_limit=10.0`), GSM8K 5-shot with only `--moe-runner-backend` varying:

| moe_runner_backend | GSM8K strict-match (runs) | mean |
|---|---|---|
| triton | 0.9356 / 0.9363 | 0.9360 |
| deep_gemm | 0.9249 / 0.9287 / 0.9295 / 0.9310 / 0.9340 / 0.9348 | 0.9305 |
| flashinfer_trtllm (before) | 0.9265 / 0.9280 / 0.9287 | 0.9277 |
| **flashinfer_trtllm (this fix)** | **0.9348 / 0.9371** | **0.9360** |

Before/after ranges do not overlap (within-group variance is ~0.2pp); after the fix flashinfer_trtllm matches the triton baseline exactly. fix https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/39797. Thx for finding this issue. @NolenLiang

## Modifications

Single-file change in `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py`, `Fp8MoEMethod._prepare_flashinfer_trtllm_activation_params()`: when `gemm1_clamp_limit` is not explicitly set, fall back to `swiglu_limit`.

## Summary

DeepEP v2 rejects 1x32 MXFP8 experts and applies routing weights before model-specific expert finalization. Support group-32 activation scales through dispatch and DeepGEMM, with unweighted route outputs and an opt-in FP32 SiLU policy for registered model architectures.

## Motivation

title: Read process groups through the runtime context (#40068)
body:
## Motivation

The same process group can be asked for in two spellings: the free accessors in
`distributed/parallel_state.py` (`get_tp_group()` and friends) and the parallel
namespace on the runtime context (`get_parallel().tp_group`). Business code uses
both, so a scope that swaps a group — the draft worker's tensor-parallel scope,
for instance — has to be installed in both places to be seen, and any later
change to how a group is answered has to be made twice.

This collects the reads onto one spelling. It does **not** remove the accessors:
they stay as the definition, so this diff is a rename and nothing else, and the
changes that do move semantics are not mixed into a whole-repo sweep.

## Modifications

323 call sites across 147 files, one commit per subsystem (`layers` → `models` →
`model executor` → `scheduler`/`disaggregation` → memory/model loading →
speculative/LoRA → elastic EP/hardware backends → utils/multimodal). Every
commit is a rename with an identical answer at every call site: the context
property falls through to the same accessor.

Deliberately **not** converted, each for a stated reason:

- **The whole `srt/distributed/` package** (81 reads). It is the layer that
  defines the accessors and builds the groups; a read there would go through the
  context back into itself.
- **`get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size()` and
  `get_attn_tensor_model_parallel_world_size()`** (9 reads). These answer with
  the *built group's* width, while `get_parallel().tp_size` / `.attn_tp_size`
  answer from the configuration. The two agree in a healthy process, but they
  are not the same question, so converting them is a behavior change rather than
  a rename. They belong with the change that makes the group build read the
  configuration and asserts the two agree.
- **`get_moe_cp_size()`** (6 reads). It is not `moe_dp_size`: the MoE-DP group is
  aliased to the attention-CP group when `attn_cp_size > moe_dp_size`, so this
  answers the real width of that communicator, which the configuration does not
  imply.
- **`get_shared_experts_tp_group()`** (1 read, in `models/kimi_k3.py`). The
  context has no name for that group, so there is nothing to rename it to.
- **`multimodal_gen/`**, which has its own parallel state.

`sglang/kernels/` is *not* excluded: its one direct reader
(`ops/layernorm/mhc.py`) is converted here too, so the accessors have no callers
outside the two exclusions above.

No module-level caching was introduced and no adjacent reads were merged: both
would freeze a live read at import time or at the wrong point in a scope.

title: [kernel] Share the warp vectorized copy and enforce its alignment (#36176)
body:
> Generated by Claude.

## Motivation

Four JIT kernels hand-rolled the same thing: a warp cooperatively moving one contiguous row. `concat_mla`, `set_mla_kv_buffer`, `store_cache` and `set_mla_kv_concat_q` each had their own vector-width selection, their own tail handling, and their own idea of what alignment they required. `warp_inclusive_sum` existed in four separate copies.

That duplication was not just untidy — it hid a bug class. The vector width a copy picks is derived from the row **size** (a 1024 B row gets 16 B accesses), but the address it lands on is `base + index * stride`, and nothing constrains a stride to match the size. Two real faults came out of that gap during this work, both reproduced:

- a `kv_buffer` row stride of 1048 B (`ROPE_DIM=12`) took 16 B stores on odd `loc` → `CUDA error: misaligned address`
- `store_cache` with `num_threads=256` on a 100 B row silently dropped the last 4 B of **every** row, because `kKBytes / kNumSplit` truncated with no guard

## What changed

**One shared copy path.** `warp::load_bytes<kBytes, kPattern>` / `store_bytes` in `warp.cuh`, backed by `LoadStorePattern`. Handles arbitrary widths down to 1 byte, including odd ones, and the ragged tail. The four hand-rolled versions are gone.

**Alignment becomes a stated precondition, not an assumption.**
- `TensorMatcher::ensure_alignment(bytes)` validates the data pointer and every stride but the innermost (size-1 dims skipped, since their strides are arbitrary).
- `LoadStorePattern::get_vec_bytes` is now `SGL_DEVICE_HOST`, so the launcher and the kernel share **one** formula. Both previous faults traced to host and kernel each hand-rolling a different `gcd`.
- The `store_cache` split carries `static_assert(kKBytes % kNumSplit == 0)`, turning the silent truncation into a compile error.

**`warp::reduce` generalised.** `<kNumThreads, kInner>` → a symmetric `<kStart, kFinish>` bit range that expresses both old modes: `<N, 1>` is the old inner reduce, `<kFullWidth, N>` the old inter-group one. Verified against an independent reference on 9 configurations.

**New primitives.** `inclusive_reduce` / `inclusive_sum` / `_max` / `_min` (with `lane_id` defaulted so the segment-relative contract can't be got wrong), `broadcast`, `atomic::Event` (cross-CTA arrive/wait in one 32-bit word), and `bits.h`.

**`get_lane_id<N>()`, per platform.** Reads the lane register on CUDA — worth 8 instructions and 2 registers in a two-tile warp copy, because the modulo form makes the compiler re-derive the mask at every address scale. On HIP it masks `threadIdx.x`, since AMD has no la …[truncated]

## Motivation

`TestFusedMOE.test_single_expert_routing` intermittently fails on H100 for

GLM-5.2 (hidden=6144, moe_intermediate_size=2048, E=256, topk=8) matches none of them, so both of its production sharding layouts - TP-8 and EP-8 without DeepEP - fall through to the generic fallback tail and run untuned.

## Modifications


Add four named branches to `dispatch_w4a8_moe_mm_sm90` for GLM-5.2's actual GEMM shapes, one per GEMM per layout:
  - TP-8: all 256 experts local, intermediate size partitioned by tp_size=8 -> gemm1 (n=512, k=6144), gemm2 (n=6144, k=256).
  - EP-8, no DeepEP: 32 experts local at the full intermediate size -> gemm1 (n=4096, k=6144), gemm2 (n=6144, k=2048).

This tuning adds four unique CUTLASS configurations, increasing the W4A8 configuration count from 12 to 16. These add compilation work and binary size.

## Accuracy Tests


Correctness is covered by `python/sglang/kernels/aot/tests/test_cutlass_w4a8_moe_mm.py`'s extended parametrization

 `test/manual/layers/moe/bench_w4a8_sm90_dispatch.py` times the complete
  `cutlass_w4a8_moe` call (preprocess/reorder/quant → GEMM1 → silu+requant →

  - **TP-8** (`mode="tp"`).

Shapes with `m<=2048` run captured under a CUDA graph, larger shapes run eager. Each shape reports median and min latency across 30 timed calls (5 warmup calls beforehand).

body:
## Motivation

Fixes #38795.

`ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoEMethod.apply` resolves the MoE backend twice from two different sources, and under speculative decoding they disagree.

`create_weights` caches it:

```python
self._moe_runner_backend = moe_runner_backend
```

`apply` reads that cache for the error message and for the marlin/megamoe checks:

```python
moe_runner_backend = getattr(self, "_moe_runner_backend", get_moe_runner_backend())
```

but the flashinfer dispatch guards re-read the **live global** instead:

```python
@property
def enable_flashinfer_cutlass_moe(self) -> bool:
    return get_moe_runner_backend().is_flashinfer_cutlass()
```

With `--speculative-moe-runner-backend`, the global is the *draft* model's backend while the target layer's cache is still the user's choice. Every flashinfer branch is skipped and the method falls through to:

```
NotImplementedError: Unsupported moe_runner_backend for NVFP4 MoE:
MoeRunnerBackend.FLASHINFER_CUTLASS. Use --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass instead.
```

The message names the backend already in use, because it prints the cache while the guard read the global.

## Repro

`nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4`, 8×B300 (sm_103), TP8/EP8:

```
--quantization modelopt_fp4 --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass
--speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 5 --speculative-eagle-topk 1
--speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 --speculative-adaptive
--speculative-moe-runner-backend triton
```

Dies at `build_adaptive_runtime_state` -> `decode_cuda_graph_runner` -> `run_moe_core` -> `modelopt_quant.apply`. Dropping `--speculative-adaptive` (fixed-step EAGLE, everything else identical) boots healthy and serves, which is why this only surfaces on the adaptive path.

## Modifications

Point the three flashinfer guards at the local `moe_runner_backend` the function already computes, matching the `is_marlin()` and `is_flashinfer_megamoe()` checks a few lines above:

```diff
-        if self.enable_flashinfer_trtllm_moe and hasattr(layer, "g1_scale_c"):
+        if moe_runner_backend.is_flashinfer_trtllm() and hasattr(layer, "g1_scale_c"):
-        if self.enable_flashinfer_cutedsl_moe:
+        if moe_runner_backend.is_flashinfer_cutedsl():
-        if self.enable_flashinfer_cutlass_moe:
+        if moe_runner_backend.is_flashinfer_cutlass():
```

The branch taken and the backend reported are now the same value by construction. A comment at the local records the invariant so the global does not creep back in.

The properties are left in place; they have other callers outside this method.

title: [ROCm] fix: remove extra bf16 -> fp32 cast in jit grouped topk kernel path (#39775)
body:
## Motivation

On ROCm with `SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_KERNEL_GROUPED_TOPK=1`, every MoE layer pays an
avoidable `bfloat16 -> float32` copy kernel on the routing bias.

`select_experts` unconditionally converts `correction_bias` into the gating dtype
whenever `_use_aiter and use_grouped_topk`:

```python
    if _use_aiter and use_grouped_topk and correction_bias is not None:
        correction_bias = topk_config.correction_bias_for_dtype(router_logits.dtype)
```

That conversion exists for `aiter_biased_grouped_topk`, which wants the bias in the
same dtype as the gating logits. But when the JIT router is enabled,
`biased_grouped_topk_gpu` returns from its `jit_grouped_gate` branch long before the
aiter branch is reached, and that branch immediately converts the bias back:

```python
        return jit_grouped_gate(
            gating_output,
            correction_bias.to(dtype=torch.float32),
            ...
        )
```

So a model that stores `e_score_correction_bias` in fp32 (GLM-5.2 does, deliberately —
its bias sits at an offset whose spread is only a few bf16 ULPs wide) gets downcast to
bf16 once, then upcast back to fp32 on **every call, for every MoE layer**. The
consumer that wanted the bf16 copy never runs.

The upcast is also redundant on its own terms: the Triton `moe_fused_gate` already
accepts a fp32/fp16/bf16 bias and `_router_triton_kernel` widens it in-register on
load, so no host-side copy is needed in either direction.

Measured on GLM-5.2-MXFP4 (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`, 78 layers, 256 routed experts),
MI355X / TP8 / conc 1 / ISL 100k / MTP: **76 extra kernel launches per target-verify
forward, 0.32 ms/step.** Each launch is ~4 us of pure launch overhead for a `[256]`
tensor.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/topk.py` — skip the downcast when the JIT grouped-topk
router is the actual consumer:

```python
    # Only aiter_biased_grouped_topk wants the bias in the gating dtype. The JIT
    # router returns before it in biased_grouped_topk_gpu and upcasts the bias
    # in-register, so downcasting here would only buy it a per-call cast back.
    if (
        _use_aiter
        and use_grouped_topk
        and correction_bias is not None
        and not envs.SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_KERNEL_GROUPED_TOPK.get()
    ):
        correction_bias = topk_config.correction_bias_for_dtype(router_logits.dtype)
```

Scope:

- `SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_KERNEL_GROUPED_TOPK` is `EnvBool(False)` by default, so the
default path is byte-for-byte unchanged — the aiter branch still receives the bias

## Summary

Replacement for #38037, which GitHub closed when its deleted support base was merged into main.

Replacement for #37629, which was accidentally squash-merged and then reverted by #37880. This reapplies the same reviewed change on the current support-branch head.

GLM-5.3-Flash ships two gfx950 MoE checkpoint paths that share one model architecture but use different quantization contracts:

- `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`: routed, shared, and MTP experts use block FP8 `[128,128]` with dynamic FP8 activations.
- `amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4`: routed and shared experts in layers 3-44 use OCP MXFP4 1×32; MTP layer 45 remains block FP8.

Both paths load gate and up projections into separate contiguous halves and require clamped SwiGLU (`swiglu_limit=10.0`). The support branch preshuffles the weights but lets AITER infer gate/up semantics from the global interleave setting. Quark also drops clamp/padding metadata and does not make preshuffle ownership explicit.

| Contract | Before | With this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| block-FP8 layout | tile-only preshuffle, no physical layout metadata | records and forwards `GateMode.SEPARATED` |
| Quark MXFP4 layout | global interleave default can override checkpoint ordering | pins separated mode; AITER preserves explicit quant-method mode |

title: [Fix] Decide the MoE padded-row bound from the layer scatter mode (#40672)
body:
## Summary

A more general fix for the truncation reported in #40643, which #39574 introduced: rather than special-casing DP attention, the bound is decided from the layer communicator's scatter mode, which also covers the non-DP and CP gathered cases and the other MoE models on the same path.

`forward_batch.num_token_non_padded` is **LOCAL** (`forward_batch_info.py`). It bounds a sparse MoE's input only while that input is this rank's own shard. On a gathered buffer each source rank contributes its own padded slot, so the real rows are not a prefix — masking with the local count drops every peer rank's tokens, and under `--moe-a2a-backend none` each rank sums a truncated partial output.

This moves that decision to `ForwardBatch.moe_num_token_non_padded()`, keyed on the scatter mode the layer communicator already computes for a sparse MLP.

**Decision table**

| MoE input | Condition | Bound |
|---|---|---|
| `SCATTERED` | a2a dispatch, FP4 all-gather, dwdp | `LOCAL` |
| `MOE_FULL` | CP extend — MoE-CP all-gather runs | none |
| `MOE_FULL` | any other forward — no gather, FULL layout | *as FULL below* |
| `FULL` | DSA / MLA CP prefill — CP all-gather, zigzag rows | none |
| `FULL` | `attn_dp_size > 1` — `dp_gather` interleaves slots | none |
| `FULL` | `attn_dp_size == 1`, attn-TP sharded — all-reduce, not gather | `GLOBAL` |
| `FULL` | `attn_dp_size == 1`, replicated | `LOCAL` |
| any | `num_token_non_padded is None` (no EP) | none |

**Changes**

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| `forward_batch_info.py` | `moe_num_token_non_padded()` — the one definition |
| `communicator.py` | `_compute_mlp_mode`'s sparse branch extracted as `sparse_mlp_scatter_mode()` |
| 17 model files + `mega_moe.py` | 24 MoE routing sites read the accessor instead of the raw field |
| `deepseek_v4.py` | inline `num_token_non_padded = None` around its MoE call dropped as redundant |
| `test_num_token_non_padded_localization.py` | table above locked; cases fail against the pre-fix behavior |

**Verification**

title: [deepep_v2] support GLM-5.3-Flash (Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration) (#40466)
body:
## Motivation

`--moe-a2a-backend deepep_v2` cannot be used with GLM-5.3-Flash
(`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`). There are two independent blockers.

**1. The architecture is not registered as v2-eligible.**
`moe_model_registry._DEEPEP_V2_MODELS` does not list it, so
`validate_deepep_v2_model_architecture()` rejects the server args before the
engine starts.

**2. `glm5_next.py` gates the a2a path on a v1-only predicate.**
`MoeA2ABackend.is_deepep()` is true only for `deepep`, not for `deepep_v2`, so
even past the first gate the model silently runs the non-a2a path:

`Glm5NextModel.__init__` computes
`enable_a2a_moe = is_deepep() or is_mooncake()`, which stays `False` under v2,
so the MoE layers never route through the dispatcher.

`deepseek_v2.py` — an already-validated v2 model — includes `is_deepep_v2()` in
that predicate. This change mirrors it.

> **Edit after review:** the first version of this PR also touched the
> `gemm_output_zero_allocator` sizing predicate and the
> shared-experts-fusion rejection reason. @mmangkad correctly pointed out that
> neither does anything here, and both are reverted as of 442125ed — see the
> Modifications section below.

## Modifications

Two lines, both load-bearing:

- `configs/moe_model_registry.py`: add `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` to
  `_DEEPEP_V2_MODELS` (`silu_mul_keep_fp32=False`, same as the other entries).
- `models/glm5_next.py`: include `is_deepep_v2()` in `enable_a2a_moe`.

title: [3/N] elastic-ep: Recapture decode CUDA graphs after scale-up (#33723)
body:
## Summary

This PR follows [PR #30553](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30553)
and adds FULL decode CUDA graph recapture after runtime Elastic EP scale-up.
Primary and joiner ranks rebuild their graphs for the expanded topology before
the new EP size is committed.

The existing scale-up API and EPLB lifecycle are unchanged.

## Changes

- Defer initial decode graph capture on joining ranks until they enter the
  expanded world.
- Finish the current sampling step, release the old graph state, and rebuild
  decode graphs with the expanded Mooncake WORLD and NIXL rank mask.
- Require primary and joiner ranks to resolve the same graph mode and capture
  configuration before recapture.
- Reuse SGLang's existing FULL decode graph initializer and synchronize all
  ranks before committing the scale operation.
- Add graph-stable FA3 MLA metadata for the validated DeepSeek path.
- Reject execution modes that do not use the supported decode finalization
  path.

## Configuration

Launch primary and joiner groups with the same resolved graph settings:

```text
--cuda-graph-backend-decode full
--cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled
--cuda-graph-bs-decode 1 2 4 8 16
```

The scale request and status API are inherited from the base scale-up PR.

## Known Limitations

- Only FULL decode graph recapture is supported. Prefill and piecewise graph
  recapture are outside this PR.
- Primary and joiner groups must use the same resolved CUDA graph
  configuration and effective capture sizes.
- Recapture is synchronous. Configuring more decode batch sizes increases the
  scale-finalization pause.
- The validated DeepSeek MLA path requires FlashAttention 3.
- Speculative decoding, embedding, diffusion, encoder-only execution, forward
  hooks, and PDMux split-prefill are not supported with Elastic EP recapture.
- The topology, scale-direction, and post-scale recovery limitations of the
  base scale-up PR still apply.
- Recapture releases the old decode graph pool before rebuilding. The deployment
  must still leave enough free GPU memory to capture the configured decode graph

## Motivation

SGLang rejects the DiffusionGemma architecture as unknown. This PR adds native BF16 text and image serving using the shared dLLM and FDFO paths from #27551 and #27877.

Fixes #29904.

## Changes

- Add the model, multimodal processor, weight loader, and Gemma4Renoise sampler, with TP1, TP2, and TP4 support.
- Encode causal context separately from each bidirectional 256-position denoising canvas, retaining request KV state across FDFO rounds and output blocks.
- Enable decode CUDA graphs with current self-conditioning embeddings and prefix-only attention metadata. Batch denoiser statistics and soft embedding work, shard the vocabulary embedding, and use the existing fused QKV normalization kernel.
- Rebase onto `db272201a2` and adapt to the current argument-resolution and request-lifecycle APIs. Keep default adaptive convergence unchanged; allow an explicit zero confidence threshold for fixed-work measurements.
- Use the checkpoint's tanh GELU in the expert layers. Fuse sampler division/argmax while retaining RNG draws, and tune H200 MoE kernels without changing precision or routing.
- Reject unsupported request fields and server settings before model execution.

- 272 tests and 64 subtests passed, including CUDA sampling/RNG equivalence, expert activation, QKV normalization, graph metadata/replay, scheduling, request lifecycle, and server arguments.

title: [NPU] Enable piecewise CUDA graph support on NPU (#28417)
body:
## Motivation

Piecewise CUDA Graph (PCG) was disabled on NPU, so NPU prefill could not use the
torch.compile-driven piecewise capture/replay path. Enabling it also requires the NPU
MoE, fused QKV/RMSNorm/RoPE, elementwise, and FLA layernorm-gated helpers to be visible
to Dynamo as traceable custom ops instead of unsupported Python or external-kernel code.

This PR enables NPU PCG behind the opt-in
`SGLANG_NPU_ENABLE_PIECEWISE_CUDA_GRAPH=1` environment variable and adds the
torch.compile compatibility needed by Qwen3/Qwen3-MoE/Qwen3.5 prefill.

## Modifications

Three commits:

**1. `[NPU] Make MoE helper ops torch.compile friendly.`**
- Register NPU weight-prefetch and CMO/shared-stream synchronization helpers as custom
  ops, separating list and single-tensor cache paths.
- Run the shared expert serially while compiling, avoiding Dynamo tracing of NPU stream
  management.
- Wrap the NPU MoE `l1_norm` helper as a custom op.
- Use a torch implementation of `fused_sigmoid_mul` during NPU compilation.
- Register the NPU fused split-QKV/RMSNorm/RoPE kernel, including its fake implementation,
  as a custom op for Qwen3 and Qwen3-MoE.
- Pass tensors through the registered stream-wait ops in Qwen2-MoE and Qwen3.

**2. `[NPU] Wrap FLA layernorm-gated op for torch.compile.`**
- Register the NPU `layer_norm_fwd` path as a custom op and declare `out` as the
  mutated argument.
- Preserve the existing `(y, mean, rstd)` return contract; the unused NPU mean/rstd
  values remain `None`.

**3. `[PCG] Enable NPU piecewise CUDA graph support.`**
- Add the `SGLANG_NPU_ENABLE_PIECEWISE_CUDA_GRAPH` opt-in and allow PCG on NPU only
  when it is enabled.
- During torch.compile warmup, execute the compiled general-shape graph directly; also
  use that path for pieces without symbolic shape inputs.
- Capture NPU graphs on the PCG capture stream with `auto_dispatch_capture=True`.
- Skip Qwen3.5 expert-distribution-recorder layer contexts only for TC-piecewise
  prefill.
- Add a registered NPU TP=2 PCG serving test for `Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B`. The test
  runs 128 requests with 4096 input tokens, concurrency 32, chunk size 2048, and

title: [Moe] Honor swiglu_limit clamped activation in flashinfer_cutlass runner (#39939)
body:
## Motivation

Models with a clamped SwiGLU activation (GLM-5 / GLM-5-Next, Qwen3-Next, GPT-OSS; configured as `swiglu_limit` or `gemm1_clamp_limit` in `MoeRunnerConfig`) silently lose the clamp on the `flashinfer_cutlass` MoE runner and run plain SwiGLU experts, for two stacked reasons: the runner's `_run_flashinfer_cutlass` never passed the per-expert SwiGLU parameters to the kernel, and its quant-info construction sites never filled them.

This path is not theoretical: on SM120 (RTX 50 series) `modelopt_fp4` is auto-pinned to `flashinfer_cutlass` because trtllm-gen MoE kernels are SM100-only (`arg_groups/overrides.py`), so NVFP4 GPT-OSS variants on SM120 hit exactly this gap today. The unquantized bf16 path is affected the same way.

For reference, the identical activation bug on the FP8 `flashinfer_trtllm` path cost GLM-5.3-Flash ~0.9pp GSM8K (92.77 -> 93.60, restored to the triton baseline; see companion PR https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39920).

## Modifications

Three files, all in the flashinfer_cutlass path; models without a configured clamp keep passing `None` and are bit-for-bit unchanged:

1. `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_cutlass.py`: add `swiglu_alpha/beta/limit` fields to `FlashInferCutlassMoeQuantInfo` (the mxfp4 sibling dataclass already had them) and pass them from `_run_flashinfer_cutlass` into `cutlass_fused_moe`.

2. `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/modelopt_quant.py` (NVFP4 + cutlass branch): fill the fields from `MoeRunnerConfig` with the same `gemm1_clamp_limit or swiglu_limit` fallback and SiTU exception already used by the ModelOpt flashinfer_trtllm branch. When a clamp is configured, alpha/beta default to the silu-neutral 1.0 / 0.0 unless the model sets `gemm1_alpha` / `gemm1_beta`.

3. `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/unquant.py` (bf16 + cutlass branch): same fill.

Unit convention: the CUTLASS kernel applies the clamp on dequantized values, so the limit is passed in physical units -- unlike trtllm-gen, where the limit must be divided by `g1_alphas` (see `modelopt_quant.py` trtllm branch). This was verified against flashinfer's own fp32-dequantized reference implementation in `tests/moe/test_trtllm_cutlass_fused_moe.py`.
